<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:松前神楽]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:松前神楽]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:松前神楽]]
'''Matsumae Kagura''' (松前神楽) is a form of {{ill|Kagura|en|Kagura|WD=Q1348260|lt=kagura|1=Kagura}} transmitted in the coastal regions along the {{ill|Sea of Japan|en|Sea of Japan|WD=Q27092|lt=Japan Sea|1=Sea of Japan}} and in the {{ill|Dounan region|ja|道南地域|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dounan region|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido|1=Hokkaido}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=https://www.town.matsumae.hokkaido.jp/bunkazai/detail/00001640.html |title=Matsumae Kagura - まつまえの文化財 文化財一覧 |access-date=2024-11-26 |publisher=松前町教育委員会}}</ref> It is a rare type of kagura that preserves a complete repertoire of performances including the {{ill|harvesting dance|ja|採物舞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/harvesting dance|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|miko dance|ja|巫女舞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/miko dance|1=miko mai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11479841}}, {{ill|hot water ritual|ja|湯立神事|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/hot water ritual|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 湯立神楽|1=yudate kagura|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11563776}}, and {{ill|Lion dance|en|Lion dance|WD=Q713866|lt=lion dance|1=Lion dance}}, and is also distinctive in that the kagura performed by [[:en:Kannushi|Shinto priests]] includes seldom-preserved pieces such as "Chitose", {{ill|Okina|ja|翁|lt=Old Man|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okina|1=okina|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11610439}} and {{ill|Sanbasou|ja|三番叟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanbasou|1=Sanbasō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11356796}}.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/411325 |title=Matsumae Kagura - 文化遺産オンライン |access-date=2024-11-26 |publisher=文化庁}}</ref> Furthermore, the repertoire and performance style suggest connections with various kagura traditions of the {{ill|Tōhoku region|en|Tōhoku region|WD=Q129465|lt=Tohoku region|1=Tōhoku region}}.<ref name=":1" />
== Overview == Matsumae Kagura is transmitted primarily by [[:en:Kannushi|Shinto priests]] in southern {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido|1=Hokkaido}}, and encompasses a diverse range of performances including the harvesting dance of {{ill|Chokumen|ja|直面|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chokumen|1=Q119379771|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q119379771}} style, miko dance, hot water ritual, lion dance, and even masked dances such as the {{ill|Okina dance|ja|翁舞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okina dance|1=Okina-mai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11610451}}. These are performed to the accompaniment of {{ill|Drum|en|Drum|WD=Q11404|lt=taiko|1=Drum}}, {{ill|Ryūteki|en|Ryūteki|WD=Q1760249|lt=ryuteki|1=Ryūteki}}, and hand-held bells ({{ill|tehira suzu|ja|手平鉦|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tehira suzu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) on a performance space of roughly one ken square.<ref name=":1" /> Although the origins of Matsumae Kagura are not clear, there is a record from {{ill|1674|en|1674|WD=Q7620|lt=1674|1=1674}} (the 2nd year of {{ill|Enpō|en|Enpō|WD=Q1145735|lt=Empo|1=Enpō}}) indicating that a {{ill|hot water kagura|ja|湯立神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/hot water kagura|1=yudate kagura|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11563776}} was performed for the first time within {{ill|Fukuyama Castle|ja|福山城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuyama Castle|1=Q11288334|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11288334}}, and a lion head donated by the lord of the {{ill|Matsumae Domain|en|Matsumae Domain|WD=Q18669712|lt=Matsumae Domain|1=Matsumae Domain}} still exists.<ref name=":1" /> In this way, Matsumae Kagura was closely associated with the Matsumae Domain. Today, it is transmitted mainly in the {{ill|Oshima region|ja|渡島地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshima region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 渡島総合振興局|1=Oshima Subprefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2226825}}, as well as in the {{ill|Hiyama region|ja|檜山地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyama region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 檜山振興局|1=Hiyama Subprefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1142537}}, the {{ill|Shiribeshi region|ja|後志地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiribeshi region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 後志支庁|1=Shiribeshi Subprefecture (1910-2010)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q839388}}, and even in {{ill|Obira, Hokkaido|en|Obira, Hokkaido|WD=Q1348684|lt=Kodaira Town|1=Obira, Hokkaido}} in the {{ill|Rumoi region|ja|留萌地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rumoi region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 留萌振興局|1=Rumoi Subprefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1151453}}. It is performed at the annual festival ({{ill|Reisai|lt=Reisai|lt=Reitaisai|ja|例祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reitaisai|qq=}}) of about 120 {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=shrines|1=Shinto shrine}}, as well as at New Year festivals and {{ill|Funatama festivals|ja|船魂|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Funatama festivals|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 船霊|1=Q11614362|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11614362}} held at shrine {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|en|Haiden (Shinto)|WD=Q3125745|lt=worship halls|1=Haiden (Shinto)}}, and is also performed in private homes upon request for purposes such as warding off misfortune ({{ill|yaku-yoke|ja|厄除け|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yaku-yoke|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 厄祓い|1=Apotropaic magic|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q620591}}) or celebrating a new construction.<ref name=":1" /> In addition, in some areas the lion dance is performed as a New Year purification ({{ill|monbarai|ja|門祓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monbarai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) by visiting local households.<ref name=":1" />
The former {{ill|Matsumae Domain|en|Matsumae Domain|WD=Q18669712|lt=Matsumae Domain|1=Matsumae Domain}}, which once had the kagura performed within its castle (thus also called "Castle Kagura" or '''Ōjō Kagura'''), saw it vigorously performed by Shinto priests during the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}}, and it later spread widely. Today, it is transmitted in a wide area including {{ill|Hakodate|en|Hakodate|WD=Q26418|lt=Hakodate City|1=Hakodate}}, {{ill|Otaru|en|Otaru|WD=Q242108|lt=Otaru City|1=Otaru}}, {{ill|Matsumae Town|ja|松前町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Town|1=松前町|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1307271}} in {{ill|Matsumae District, Hokkaido|en|Matsumae District, Hokkaido|WD=Q1145821|lt=Matsumae District|1=Matsumae District, Hokkaido}}, and {{ill|Fukushima, Hokkaido|en|Fukushima, Hokkaido|WD=Q1354260|lt=Fukushima Town|1=Fukushima, Hokkaido}}, as well as in other parts of the Japan Sea coastal regions and the Dounan area of Hokkaido, and is publicly performed at shrine major festivals.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/137157 |title=Matsumae Kagura - 文化遺産オンライン |access-date=2024-11-26 |publisher=文化庁}}</ref>
== History == The origins of Matsumae Kagura are variously explained and remain uncertain.<ref name=":0" /> According to the official chronicle of the {{ill|Matsumae Family|ja|松前家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Family|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 蠣崎氏|1=Kakizaki clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q15734194}}, as recorded in the {{ill|Shinra no Kiroku|en|Shinra no Kiroku|WD=Q17218176|lt=Shinra no Kiroku|1=Shinra no Kiroku}}, in {{ill|1625|en|1625|WD=Q6826|lt=1625|1=1625}} (the 2nd year of {{ill|Kan'ei|en|Kan'ei|WD=Q1192913|lt=Kanei|1=Kan'ei}}) when the {{ill|Hachiman shrine|en|Hachiman shrine|WD=Q11390939|lt=Hachiman Shrine|1=Hachiman shrine}} that had been located in Ōdate was relocated to Fukuyama, records mention the construction of a treasure hall, a worship hall, and the building of a "Kaguraya" (kagura hall). Whether the kagura performed in that "Kaguraya" is the same as the Matsumae Kagura transmitted today is not certain, but it is clear that kagura was already practiced within the territory of the Matsumae Domain at that time.<ref name=":0" /> According to the "Fukuyama Hifu", in {{ill|1974|en|1974|WD=Q2478|lt=1974|1=1974}} (the 2nd year of {{ill|Enpō|en|Enpō|WD=Q1145735|lt=Empo|1=Enpō}}) during the era of the 10th lord of the Matsumae Domain, {{ill|Matsumae Norihiro|ja|松前矩廣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Norihiro|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the "Shizugama Yudate Kagura" was performed for the first time as an official event inside Fukuyama Castle. Since then, the kagura has been performed every other year in the castle’s spear hall under the patronage of the Matsumae Domain’s lord.<ref name=":0" /> Furthermore, according to the "Gojōnai Daijinji" established in {{ill|1681|en|1681|WD=Q7645|lt=1681|1=1681}} (the 9th year of {{ill|Enpō|en|Enpō|WD=Q1145735|lt=Empo|1=Enpō}}), it is evident that 23 divine rituals and dances, beginning with the "Gokito" (prayer ritual), were already in existence at that time.<ref name=":0" />
Subsequently, the kagura form was further refined, and today it is composed of 12 divine rituals and 21 dances.<ref name=":0" /> Matsumae Kagura was passed down in an hereditary manner by the shrine families within the Matsumae Domain, who strictly preserved the ancient traditions and developed the art into a dignified form of ritual performance.<ref name=":0" /> At the same time, Matsumae Kagura was greatly supported by the common people.<ref name=":0" /> People, for their own benefit, performed various kagura prayers ({{ill|kito|ja|祈祷|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祈り|1=Prayer|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q40953}}) such as the {{ill|herring field kagura|ja|ニシン場|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/herring field kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the {{ill|salmon field abundant harvest kagura|ja|鮭場豊漁神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/salmon field abundant harvest kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the {{ill|fairground safety kagura|ja|会場安全神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fairground safety kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the {{ill|small-boat new construction kagura|ja|手船新造神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/small-boat new construction kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the {{ill|fire-extinguishing kagura|ja|火災消滅神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fire-extinguishing kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the {{ill|smallpox safety kagura|ja|疱瘡安全神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/smallpox safety kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, wishing for safe journeys, abundant harvests, and the dispelling of epidemics.<ref name=":0" /> When the patronage of the Matsumae Domain was lost during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}}, the shrine families who had preserved Matsumae Kagura deepened their ties with the parishioners, and the tradition has been transmitted up to the present day.<ref name=":0" /> Moreover, people freed from the constraints of the feudal han system migrated throughout Hokkaido in search of abundant fishing resources, and in the midst of harsh living conditions, they established Matsumae Kagura as a familiar cultural practice from childhood in their new communities.<ref name=":0" />
Since the Meiji period, Matsumae Kagura has been performed throughout the Japan Sea coastal regions, especially in the {{ill|Oshima region|ja|渡島地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshima region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 渡島総合振興局|1=Oshima Subprefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2226825}}.<ref name=":0" /> However, over time, subtle regional differences have emerged in Matsumae Kagura.<ref name=":0" /> Today, block preservation associations have been formed in the four regions of Matsumae, Fukushima, Hakodate, and Otaru, each working to preserve and transmit its unique tradition.<ref name=":0" /> On March 8, {{ill|2018|en|2018|WD=Q25291|lt=2018|1=2018}}, it was designated as an {{ill|Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|重要無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|1=National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6573893}}.<ref name=":0" />
== Repertoire == [[File:Kuruma_okina_mai.jpg|alt=翁舞（The image is not of Matsumae Kagura but of the Kuruma Okina Mai [ja]）|thumb]] The repertoire of Matsumae Kagura is extensive, as listed below. Although the content and names of the pieces vary slightly between transmission areas, all share a strong ritual and ceremonial character with minimal emphasis on mere entertainment.<ref name=":2" /> It is said that because the former lord of the Matsumae Domain was originally from the {{ill|Wakasa region|ja|若狭地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 嶺南|1=Reinan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11477418}} of {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|en|Fukui Prefecture|WD=Q133879|lt=Fukui Prefecture|1=Fukui Prefecture}}, there are connections with the dance music of Kyoto and the kagura of the {{ill|Izumo region|ja|出雲地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 出雲|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}}, and also direct influences from the mountain ascetic kagura and variety performances of the {{ill|Tōhoku region|en|Tōhoku region|WD=Q129465|lt=Tohoku region|1=Tōhoku region}}.<ref name=":2" /> Thus, Matsumae Kagura, which has preserved a tradition in Hokkaido since the Edo period and has been widely performed with regional characteristics added throughout the island, is an important example illustrating the evolution of performing arts and regional traits.<ref name=":2" />
* '''Sakaki Mai''' (さかきまい) – A dance in which the officiant moves gracefully to the right, left, forward, and backward while performing in a quiet manner, symbolically purifying the sacred precinct by entering the inner court of the shrine in the morning and evening, and offering the {{ill|Gohei|en|Gohei|WD=Q1011372|lt=gohei|1=Gohei}} as an expression of divine service by the Shinto priest.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/%e6%9d%be%e5%89%8d%e7%a5%9e%e6%a5%bd%e3%83%bb%e8%b1%86%e7%9f%a5%e8%ad%98%e3%80%80%e6%a6%8a%e8%88%9e%ef%bc%88%e3%81%95%e3%81%8b%e3%81%8d%e3%81%be%e3%81%84%ef%bc%89/ |title=Matsumae Kagura – Tidbits: Sakaki Mai (さかきまい) |access-date=2024-11-28 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> In various regions, it is also called "Heihaku Mai" or "Norito Mai". This kagura was personally developed by the Matsumae Domain and its lord.<ref name=":3" /> * '''Suzue''' (すずあげ) – A dance in which the dancer holds a {{ill|bell|ja|鈴|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/bell|1=suzu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q7651136}} and a {{ill|fan|ja|扇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fan|1=Q108778988|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108778988}}, frequently raising and lowering the bell during the performance; it is said to depict the descent of a {{ill|celestial maiden|ja|天女|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/celestial maiden|qq=}}. As it is performed by girls under their teenage years, it is also known as "Otome Mai" or "Miko Mai".<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-155/ |title=Matsumae Kagura – Tidbits: Suzue (Miko Dance) |access-date=2024-11-28 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''Fukuden Mai''' (ふくでんまい) – A dance in which the performer holds sacred banners in both hands and purifies all four corners. Accompanied by the shout "Haayo!" the dancer treads on fields to symbolize solidifying them while praying for a bountiful harvest of the five grains. It is also known as "Atoharai" because it is performed at the end of evening festivals where a lion dance is not held.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-109/ |title=Matsumae Kagura – Tidbits: Fukuden Mai (ふくでんまい) |access-date=2024-11-28 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> The music and divine songs of Fukuden Mai are also used in other pieces. * '''Niwa Sagomai''' (にわさごまい) – Also known as "Niwa Sangomai" or "Torianakomai", this dance portrays a rooster, considered a sacred bird that heralds the opening of the heavenly rock door to announce the arrival of light after darkness, and that treads firmly upon the earth at the beginning of the world ({{ill|Zuitori|ja|瑞鳥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zuitori|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 瑞獣|1=Q11573922|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11573922}}). The dancer wears a crown with two bird figures (male and female); the male’s feathers symbolize auspicious clouds (heaven) and the female’s represent ocean waves (earth), expressing the harmony between the sexes and celebrating a peaceful world by scattering the divine rice that signifies the abundant harvest of the "land of the auspicious grain" lasting fifteen hundred autumns.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-1571/ |title=Matsumae Kagura on a luxury liner – Niwa Sagomai |access-date=2024-11-18 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''Shika Sagomai''' (しかさごまい) – A dance performed when a shrine’s buildings or its {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|WD=Q234731|lt=torii|1=Torii}} are newly constructed. It is a custom mainly found in southern Hokkaido and is also called "Sanpin Mai" or "Sanshu Mai".<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-1484/ |title=[Video] Matsumae Kagura Joint Performance – Shika Sagomai |access-date=2024-11-28 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''Sanbasou Mai''' (さんばそうまい) – A dance performed by a short, dark-faced, vigorous old man who symbolizes robust health, longevity, and moral rectitude. He celebrates his own long life and the prosperity of his family by dancing joyfully in honor of his talented descendants, blessing the flourishing of his lineage.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-1549/ |title=Matsumae Kagura on a luxury liner – Sanbasou Mai |access-date=2024-11-28 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''Okina Mai''' (翁舞) – A dance in which a humorous, tall, and gentle old man, despite his wrinkled forehead, demonstrates physical strength acquired over many years, and during the performance expresses his wishes in words, celebrating longevity, career success, and prosperity, embodying the blessings of the deities of longevity and fortune.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-1574/ |title=Matsumae Kagura on a luxury liner – Okina Mai |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''Kami Asobi Mai''' (かみあそびまい) – A dance in which two warriors armed with bows and arrows expel malevolent spirits from all directions and restore a rightful state of mind. It was intended to demonstrate the virtue of the Matsumae Domain both internally and externally, and to pray for the pacification of {{ill|Ezo|en|Ezo|WD=Q1040184|lt=Ezochi|1=Ezo}} and universal peace. This dance is traditionally attributed to the 6th lord of the Matsumae Domain, {{ill|Matsumae Norihiro|ja|矩広|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Norihiro|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and is also known as "Tenno Asobi Mai".<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |url=https://gongensan.jp/KAGURA/%E6%9D%BE%E5%89%8D%E7%A5%9E%E6%A5%BD-%E5%85%B6%E3%83%8E%E4%BA%8C/ |title=Matsumae Kagura, Part II |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=権現山内浦神社}}</ref> * '''Shichigosan Harai Mai''' (しめはらいまい) – A dance in which a sword is used to purify all four directions, symbolically expelling evil spirits.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-129/ |title=Fukushima Town/ Shirofu Ōjin Shrine Festival: Matsumae Kagura "Shichigosan Harai Mai" (Heisei 19) |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''{{ill|Lion dance|en|Lion dance|WD=Q713866|lt=Shishi Mai|1=Lion dance}}''' (ししまい) – A lion dance that exists in various forms such as "Twelve-handed Shishi Mai", "Onryōi Mai", "Gohō", "Shishi no Suzuage", and "Men Ashi Shishi (Sasara)".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/%e3%80%90%e6%9d%be%e5%89%8d%e7%a5%9e%e6%a5%bd%e3%80%91%e5%8d%81%e4%ba%8c%e3%81%ae%e6%89%8b%e7%8d%85%e5%ad%90%e8%88%9e%e3%83%bb%e4%ba%94%e6%96%b9%e3%80%80%e5%86%99%e7%9c%9f/ |title=[Matsumae Kagura] Twelve-handed Shishi Mai & Gohō – Photographs |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref>
== Transmission == === Regions === Matsumae Kagura is transmitted in a wide area including the Japan Sea coastal regions and the Dounan area of {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido|1=Hokkaido}}, and subtle regional differences have emerged over time.<ref name=":0" /> Block preservation associations have been established in the four regions of Matsumae, Fukushima, Hakodate, and Otaru, each working to preserve and pass on its tradition.<ref name=":0" /> Performances are held at shrine festivals and local event venues throughout Hokkaido (with schedules varying by region). In Matsumae Town, a public performance of Matsumae Kagura is held annually on {{ill|April 29|en|April 29|WD=Q2535|lt=April 29|1=April 29}} at the Honmaru Plaza of {{ill|Matsumae Park|ja|松前公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Park|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 松前城|1=Matsumae Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1143974}}.<ref name=":0" /> The following is a list of municipalities where Matsumae Kagura is mainly transmitted.<ref name=":1" />
{{Columns-list|20em| * {{ill|Hakodate|en|Hakodate|WD=Q26418|lt=Hakodate City|1=Hakodate}} * {{ill|Otaru|en|Otaru|WD=Q242108|lt=Otaru City|1=Otaru}} * {{ill|Hokuto, Hokkaido|en|Hokuto, Hokkaido|WD=Q842301|lt=Hokuto City|1=Hokuto, Hokkaido}} * {{ill|Matsumae Town|ja|松前町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Town|1=松前町|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1307271}} * Town|1=Suttsu, Hokkaido}} * {{ill|Kuromatsunai, Hokkaido|en|Kuromatsunai, Hokkaido|WD=Q1355464|lt=Kuromatsunai Town|1=Kuromatsunai, Hokkaido}} * {{ill|Rankoshi, Hokkaido|en|Rankoshi, Hokkaido|WD=Q1355416|lt=Rankoshi Town|1=Rankoshi, Hokkaido}} * {{ill|Kimobetsu, Hokkaido|en|Kimobetsu, Hokkaido|WD=Q1355478|lt=Kimobetsu Town|1=Kimobetsu, Hokkaido}} * {{ill|Kyōgoku, Hokkaido|en|Kyōwa, Hokkaido|WD=Q1354347|lt=Kyowa Town|1=Kyōwa, Hokkaido}} * {{ill|Iwanai, Hokkaido|en|Iwanai, Hokkaido|WD=Q1354481|lt=Iwanai Town|1=Iwanai, Hokkaido}} * {{ill|Tomari, Hokkaido|en|Niki, Hokkaido|WD=Q1354360|lt=Niki Town|1=Niki, Hokkaido}} * {{ill|Obira, Hokkaido|en|Obira, Hokkaido|WD=Q1348684|lt=Kodaira Town|1=Obira, Hokkaido}} }}
=== Preservation and Transmission === Matsumae Kagura was designated as an {{ill|Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|重要無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|1=National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6573893}} on March 8, {{ill|2018|en|2018|WD=Q25291|lt=2018|1=2018}}.<ref name=":0" /> It is being preserved and transmitted under the auspices of the Matsumae Kagura Hokkaido United Preservation Association, together with the Hakodate United Preservation Association, the Otaru Block Preservation Association, the Matsumae Block United Preservation Association, and the Fukushima Town Matsumae Kagura Preservation Association.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |url=https://www.siomigaoka.com/matumaekagura |title=Matsumae Kagura (Matsumae Kagura Otaru Preservation Association) |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=潮見ヶ岡神社}}</ref>
In {{ill|1958|en|1958|WD=Q5253|lt=1958|1=1958}} (Showa 33), 12 performers were designated as holders of Hokkaido's intangible cultural properties, with 4 designated in each of the three blocks (Otaru, Fukushima, and Matsumae).<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/kagura-history/ |title=About Matsumae Kagura |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> In {{ill|1968|en|1968|WD=Q2644|lt=1968|1=1968}} (Showa 43), a statewide organization called the "Matsumae Kagura United Preservation Association" was established, and subsequently in {{ill|1995|en|1995|WD=Q2068|lt=1995|1=1995}} (Heisei 7) it was selected by the national government as a "folk cultural material for which measures for documentation should be taken." To further consolidate efforts toward designation as a national intangible cultural property, the Matsumae Kagura Preservation Association was dissolved in {{ill|1999|en|1999|WD=Q2091|lt=1999|1=1999}} (Heisei 11) and replaced by the "Hokkaido Matsumae Kagura Preservation Association" (an umbrella organization comprising the Hakodate, Matsumae Block, Otaru Block, and Fukushima Town preservation associations).<ref name=":10" /> In {{ill|2008|en|2008|WD=Q2004|lt=2008|1=2008}} (Heisei 20), following the death of the last designated holder, Osamu Kimura, the designation under Hokkaido's system was cancelled; however, in June of that year a new designation was granted to the Hokkaido Matsumae Kagura United Preservation Association (covering 4 blocks). Finally, in {{ill|2018|en|2018|WD=Q25291|lt=2018|1=2018}} (Heisei 30) it was designated as a national {{ill|Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|重要無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|1=National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6573893}}.<ref name=":10" />
Below is the timeline of events leading up to its national designation:<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":10" /> * {{ill|1958|en|1958|WD=Q5253|lt=1958|1=1958}} (Showa 33) – Designated as the first Hokkaido intangible cultural property, with 12 holders recognized. * {{ill|1995|en|1995|WD=Q2068|lt=1995|1=1995}} (Heisei 7) – Selected by the national government as a "folk cultural material for which measures for documentation should be taken" (documentary selection). * {{ill|1999|en|1999|WD=Q2091|lt=1999|1=1999}} (Heisei 11) – The Matsumae Kagura United Preservation Association was formed in anticipation of national designation as an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property. * {{ill|2008|en|2008|WD=Q2004|lt=2008|1=2008}} (Heisei 20) – Following the death of the last holder, the Hokkaido designation was cancelled; subsequently, it was designated as a Hokkaido intangible folk cultural property with the preservation associations and their four subordinate groups clearly stated. * {{ill|2018|en|2018|WD=Q25291|lt=2018|1=2018}} (Heisei 30) – Designated as a national {{ill|Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|重要無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|1=National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6573893}}.

'''Matsumae Kagura''' (松前神楽) is a form of {{ill|Kagura|en|Kagura|WD=Q1348260|lt=kagura|1=Kagura}} transmitted in the coastal regions along the {{ill|Sea of Japan|en|Sea of Japan|WD=Q27092|lt=Japan Sea|1=Sea of Japan}} and in the {{ill|Dounan region|ja|道南地域|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dounan region|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido|1=Hokkaido}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=https://www.town.matsumae.hokkaido.jp/bunkazai/detail/00001640.html |title=Matsumae Kagura - まつまえの文化財 文化財一覧 |access-date=2024-11-26 |publisher=松前町教育委員会}}</ref> It is a rare type of kagura that preserves a complete repertoire of performances including the {{ill|harvesting dance|ja|採物舞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/harvesting dance|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|miko dance|ja|巫女舞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/miko dance|1=miko mai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11479841}}, {{ill|hot water ritual|ja|湯立神事|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/hot water ritual|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 湯立神楽|1=yudate kagura|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11563776}}, and {{ill|Lion dance|en|Lion dance|WD=Q713866|lt=lion dance|1=Lion dance}}, and is also distinctive in that the kagura performed by [[:en:Kannushi|Shinto priests]] includes seldom-preserved pieces such as "Chitose", {{ill|Okina|ja|翁|lt=Old Man|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okina|1=okina|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11610439}} and {{ill|Sanbasou|ja|三番叟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanbasou|1=Sanbasō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11356796}}.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/411325 |title=Matsumae Kagura - 文化遺産オンライン |access-date=2024-11-26 |publisher=文化庁}}</ref> Furthermore, the repertoire and performance style suggest connections with various kagura traditions of the {{ill|Tōhoku region|en|Tōhoku region|WD=Q129465|lt=Tohoku region|1=Tōhoku region}}.<ref name=":1" />
== Overview == Matsumae Kagura is transmitted primarily by [[:en:Kannushi|Shinto priests]] in southern {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido|1=Hokkaido}}, and encompasses a diverse range of performances including the harvesting dance of {{ill|Chokumen|ja|直面|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chokumen|1=Q119379771|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q119379771}} style, miko dance, hot water ritual, lion dance, and even masked dances such as the {{ill|Okina dance|ja|翁舞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okina dance|1=Okina-mai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11610451}}. These are performed to the accompaniment of {{ill|Drum|en|Drum|WD=Q11404|lt=taiko|1=Drum}}, {{ill|Ryūteki|en|Ryūteki|WD=Q1760249|lt=ryuteki|1=Ryūteki}}, and hand-held bells ({{ill|tehira suzu|ja|手平鉦|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tehira suzu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) on a performance space of roughly one ken square.<ref name=":1" /> Although the origins of Matsumae Kagura are not clear, there is a record from {{ill|1674|en|1674|WD=Q7620|lt=1674|1=1674}} (the 2nd year of {{ill|Enpō|en|Enpō|WD=Q1145735|lt=Empo|1=Enpō}}) indicating that a {{ill|hot water kagura|ja|湯立神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/hot water kagura|1=yudate kagura|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11563776}} was performed for the first time within {{ill|Fukuyama Castle|ja|福山城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuyama Castle|1=Q11288334|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11288334}}, and a lion head donated by the lord of the {{ill|Matsumae Domain|en|Matsumae Domain|WD=Q18669712|lt=Matsumae Domain|1=Matsumae Domain}} still exists.<ref name=":1" /> In this way, Matsumae Kagura was closely associated with the Matsumae Domain. Today, it is transmitted mainly in the {{ill|Oshima region|ja|渡島地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshima region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 渡島総合振興局|1=Oshima Subprefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2226825}}, as well as in the {{ill|Hiyama region|ja|檜山地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyama region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 檜山振興局|1=Hiyama Subprefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1142537}}, the {{ill|Shiribeshi region|ja|後志地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiribeshi region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 後志支庁|1=Shiribeshi Subprefecture (1910-2010)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q839388}}, and even in {{ill|Obira, Hokkaido|en|Obira, Hokkaido|WD=Q1348684|lt=Kodaira Town|1=Obira, Hokkaido}} in the {{ill|Rumoi region|ja|留萌地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rumoi region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 留萌振興局|1=Rumoi Subprefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1151453}}. It is performed at the annual festival ({{ill|Reisai|lt=Reisai|lt=Reitaisai|ja|例祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reitaisai|qq=}}) of about 120 {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=shrines|1=Shinto shrine}}, as well as at New Year festivals and {{ill|Funatama festivals|ja|船魂|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Funatama festivals|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 船霊|1=Q11614362|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11614362}} held at shrine {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|en|Haiden (Shinto)|WD=Q3125745|lt=worship halls|1=Haiden (Shinto)}}, and is also performed in private homes upon request for purposes such as warding off misfortune ({{ill|yaku-yoke|ja|厄除け|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yaku-yoke|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 厄祓い|1=Apotropaic magic|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q620591}}) or celebrating a new construction.<ref name=":1" /> In addition, in some areas the lion dance is performed as a New Year purification ({{ill|monbarai|ja|門祓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monbarai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) by visiting local households.<ref name=":1" />
The former {{ill|Matsumae Domain|en|Matsumae Domain|WD=Q18669712|lt=Matsumae Domain|1=Matsumae Domain}}, which once had the kagura performed within its castle (thus also called "Castle Kagura" or '''Ōjō Kagura'''), saw it vigorously performed by Shinto priests during the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}}, and it later spread widely. Today, it is transmitted in a wide area including {{ill|Hakodate|en|Hakodate|WD=Q26418|lt=Hakodate City|1=Hakodate}}, {{ill|Otaru|en|Otaru|WD=Q242108|lt=Otaru City|1=Otaru}}, {{ill|Matsumae Town|ja|松前町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Town|1=松前町|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1307271}} in {{ill|Matsumae District, Hokkaido|en|Matsumae District, Hokkaido|WD=Q1145821|lt=Matsumae District|1=Matsumae District, Hokkaido}}, and {{ill|Fukushima, Hokkaido|en|Fukushima, Hokkaido|WD=Q1354260|lt=Fukushima Town|1=Fukushima, Hokkaido}}, as well as in other parts of the Japan Sea coastal regions and the Dounan area of Hokkaido, and is publicly performed at shrine major festivals.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/137157 |title=Matsumae Kagura - 文化遺産オンライン |access-date=2024-11-26 |publisher=文化庁}}</ref>
== History == The origins of Matsumae Kagura are variously explained and remain uncertain.<ref name=":0" /> According to the official chronicle of the {{ill|Matsumae Family|ja|松前家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Family|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 蠣崎氏|1=Kakizaki clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q15734194}}, as recorded in the {{ill|Shinra no Kiroku|en|Shinra no Kiroku|WD=Q17218176|lt=Shinra no Kiroku|1=Shinra no Kiroku}}, in {{ill|1625|en|1625|WD=Q6826|lt=1625|1=1625}} (the 2nd year of {{ill|Kan'ei|en|Kan'ei|WD=Q1192913|lt=Kanei|1=Kan'ei}}) when the {{ill|Hachiman shrine|en|Hachiman shrine|WD=Q11390939|lt=Hachiman Shrine|1=Hachiman shrine}} that had been located in Ōdate was relocated to Fukuyama, records mention the construction of a treasure hall, a worship hall, and the building of a "Kaguraya" (kagura hall). Whether the kagura performed in that "Kaguraya" is the same as the Matsumae Kagura transmitted today is not certain, but it is clear that kagura was already practiced within the territory of the Matsumae Domain at that time.<ref name=":0" /> According to the "Fukuyama Hifu", in {{ill|1974|en|1974|WD=Q2478|lt=1974|1=1974}} (the 2nd year of {{ill|Enpō|en|Enpō|WD=Q1145735|lt=Empo|1=Enpō}}) during the era of the 10th lord of the Matsumae Domain, {{ill|Matsumae Norihiro|ja|松前矩廣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Norihiro|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the "Shizugama Yudate Kagura" was performed for the first time as an official event inside Fukuyama Castle. Since then, the kagura has been performed every other year in the castle’s spear hall under the patronage of the Matsumae Domain’s lord.<ref name=":0" /> Furthermore, according to the "Gojōnai Daijinji" established in {{ill|1681|en|1681|WD=Q7645|lt=1681|1=1681}} (the 9th year of {{ill|Enpō|en|Enpō|WD=Q1145735|lt=Empo|1=Enpō}}), it is evident that 23 divine rituals and dances, beginning with the "Gokito" (prayer ritual), were already in existence at that time.<ref name=":0" />
Subsequently, the kagura form was further refined, and today it is composed of 12 divine rituals and 21 dances.<ref name=":0" /> Matsumae Kagura was passed down in an hereditary manner by the shrine families within the Matsumae Domain, who strictly preserved the ancient traditions and developed the art into a dignified form of ritual performance.<ref name=":0" /> At the same time, Matsumae Kagura was greatly supported by the common people.<ref name=":0" /> People, for their own benefit, performed various kagura prayers ({{ill|kito|ja|祈祷|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祈り|1=Prayer|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q40953}}) such as the {{ill|herring field kagura|ja|ニシン場|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/herring field kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the {{ill|salmon field abundant harvest kagura|ja|鮭場豊漁神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/salmon field abundant harvest kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the {{ill|fairground safety kagura|ja|会場安全神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fairground safety kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the {{ill|small-boat new construction kagura|ja|手船新造神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/small-boat new construction kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the {{ill|fire-extinguishing kagura|ja|火災消滅神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fire-extinguishing kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the {{ill|smallpox safety kagura|ja|疱瘡安全神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/smallpox safety kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, wishing for safe journeys, abundant harvests, and the dispelling of epidemics.<ref name=":0" /> When the patronage of the Matsumae Domain was lost during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}}, the shrine families who had preserved Matsumae Kagura deepened their ties with the parishioners, and the tradition has been transmitted up to the present day.<ref name=":0" /> Moreover, people freed from the constraints of the feudal han system migrated throughout Hokkaido in search of abundant fishing resources, and in the midst of harsh living conditions, they established Matsumae Kagura as a familiar cultural practice from childhood in their new communities.<ref name=":0" />
Since the Meiji period, Matsumae Kagura has been performed throughout the Japan Sea coastal regions, especially in the {{ill|Oshima region|ja|渡島地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshima region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 渡島総合振興局|1=Oshima Subprefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2226825}}.<ref name=":0" /> However, over time, subtle regional differences have emerged in Matsumae Kagura.<ref name=":0" /> Today, block preservation associations have been formed in the four regions of Matsumae, Fukushima, Hakodate, and Otaru, each working to preserve and transmit its unique tradition.<ref name=":0" /> On March 8, {{ill|2018|en|2018|WD=Q25291|lt=2018|1=2018}}, it was designated as an {{ill|Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|重要無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|1=National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6573893}}.<ref name=":0" />
== Repertoire == [[File:Kuruma_okina_mai.jpg|alt=翁舞（The image is not of Matsumae Kagura but of the Kuruma Okina Mai [ja]）|thumb]] The repertoire of Matsumae Kagura is extensive, as listed below. Although the content and names of the pieces vary slightly between transmission areas, all share a strong ritual and ceremonial character with minimal emphasis on mere entertainment.<ref name=":2" /> It is said that because the former lord of the Matsumae Domain was originally from the {{ill|Wakasa region|ja|若狭地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 嶺南|1=Reinan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11477418}} of {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|en|Fukui Prefecture|WD=Q133879|lt=Fukui Prefecture|1=Fukui Prefecture}}, there are connections with the dance music of Kyoto and the kagura of the {{ill|Izumo region|ja|出雲地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 出雲|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}}, and also direct influences from the mountain ascetic kagura and variety performances of the {{ill|Tōhoku region|en|Tōhoku region|WD=Q129465|lt=Tohoku region|1=Tōhoku region}}.<ref name=":2" /> Thus, Matsumae Kagura, which has preserved a tradition in Hokkaido since the Edo period and has been widely performed with regional characteristics added throughout the island, is an important example illustrating the evolution of performing arts and regional traits.<ref name=":2" />
* '''Sakaki Mai''' (さかきまい) – A dance in which the officiant moves gracefully to the right, left, forward, and backward while performing in a quiet manner, symbolically purifying the sacred precinct by entering the inner court of the shrine in the morning and evening, and offering the {{ill|Gohei|en|Gohei|WD=Q1011372|lt=gohei|1=Gohei}} as an expression of divine service by the Shinto priest.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/%e6%9d%be%e5%89%8d%e7%a5%9e%e6%a5%bd%e3%83%bb%e8%b1%86%e7%9f%a5%e8%ad%98%e3%80%80%e6%a6%8a%e8%88%9e%ef%bc%88%e3%81%95%e3%81%8b%e3%81%8d%e3%81%be%e3%81%84%ef%bc%89/ |title=Matsumae Kagura – Tidbits: Sakaki Mai (さかきまい) |access-date=2024-11-28 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> In various regions, it is also called "Heihaku Mai" or "Norito Mai". This kagura was personally developed by the Matsumae Domain and its lord.<ref name=":3" /> * '''Suzue''' (すずあげ) – A dance in which the dancer holds a {{ill|bell|ja|鈴|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/bell|1=suzu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q7651136}} and a {{ill|fan|ja|扇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fan|1=Q108778988|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108778988}}, frequently raising and lowering the bell during the performance; it is said to depict the descent of a {{ill|celestial maiden|ja|天女|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/celestial maiden|qq=}}. As it is performed by girls under their teenage years, it is also known as "Otome Mai" or "Miko Mai".<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-155/ |title=Matsumae Kagura – Tidbits: Suzue (Miko Dance) |access-date=2024-11-28 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''Fukuden Mai''' (ふくでんまい) – A dance in which the performer holds sacred banners in both hands and purifies all four corners. Accompanied by the shout "Haayo!" the dancer treads on fields to symbolize solidifying them while praying for a bountiful harvest of the five grains. It is also known as "Atoharai" because it is performed at the end of evening festivals where a lion dance is not held.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-109/ |title=Matsumae Kagura – Tidbits: Fukuden Mai (ふくでんまい) |access-date=2024-11-28 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> The music and divine songs of Fukuden Mai are also used in other pieces. * '''Niwa Sagomai''' (にわさごまい) – Also known as "Niwa Sangomai" or "Torianakomai", this dance portrays a rooster, considered a sacred bird that heralds the opening of the heavenly rock door to announce the arrival of light after darkness, and that treads firmly upon the earth at the beginning of the world ({{ill|Zuitori|ja|瑞鳥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zuitori|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 瑞獣|1=Q11573922|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11573922}}). The dancer wears a crown with two bird figures (male and female); the male’s feathers symbolize auspicious clouds (heaven) and the female’s represent ocean waves (earth), expressing the harmony between the sexes and celebrating a peaceful world by scattering the divine rice that signifies the abundant harvest of the "land of the auspicious grain" lasting fifteen hundred autumns.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-1571/ |title=Matsumae Kagura on a luxury liner – Niwa Sagomai |access-date=2024-11-18 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''Shika Sagomai''' (しかさごまい) – A dance performed when a shrine’s buildings or its {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|WD=Q234731|lt=torii|1=Torii}} are newly constructed. It is a custom mainly found in southern Hokkaido and is also called "Sanpin Mai" or "Sanshu Mai".<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-1484/ |title=[Video] Matsumae Kagura Joint Performance – Shika Sagomai |access-date=2024-11-28 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''Sanbasou Mai''' (さんばそうまい) – A dance performed by a short, dark-faced, vigorous old man who symbolizes robust health, longevity, and moral rectitude. He celebrates his own long life and the prosperity of his family by dancing joyfully in honor of his talented descendants, blessing the flourishing of his lineage.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-1549/ |title=Matsumae Kagura on a luxury liner – Sanbasou Mai |access-date=2024-11-28 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''Okina Mai''' (翁舞) – A dance in which a humorous, tall, and gentle old man, despite his wrinkled forehead, demonstrates physical strength acquired over many years, and during the performance expresses his wishes in words, celebrating longevity, career success, and prosperity, embodying the blessings of the deities of longevity and fortune.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-1574/ |title=Matsumae Kagura on a luxury liner – Okina Mai |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''Kami Asobi Mai''' (かみあそびまい) – A dance in which two warriors armed with bows and arrows expel malevolent spirits from all directions and restore a rightful state of mind. It was intended to demonstrate the virtue of the Matsumae Domain both internally and externally, and to pray for the pacification of {{ill|Ezo|en|Ezo|WD=Q1040184|lt=Ezochi|1=Ezo}} and universal peace. This dance is traditionally attributed to the 6th lord of the Matsumae Domain, {{ill|Matsumae Norihiro|ja|矩広|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Norihiro|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and is also known as "Tenno Asobi Mai".<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |url=https://gongensan.jp/KAGURA/%E6%9D%BE%E5%89%8D%E7%A5%9E%E6%A5%BD-%E5%85%B6%E3%83%8E%E4%BA%8C/ |title=Matsumae Kagura, Part II |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=権現山内浦神社}}</ref> * '''Shichigosan Harai Mai''' (しめはらいまい) – A dance in which a sword is used to purify all four directions, symbolically expelling evil spirits.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-129/ |title=Fukushima Town/ Shirofu Ōjin Shrine Festival: Matsumae Kagura "Shichigosan Harai Mai" (Heisei 19) |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''{{ill|Lion dance|en|Lion dance|WD=Q713866|lt=Shishi Mai|1=Lion dance}}''' (ししまい) – A lion dance that exists in various forms such as "Twelve-handed Shishi Mai", "Onryōi Mai", "Gohō", "Shishi no Suzuage", and "Men Ashi Shishi (Sasara)".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/%e3%80%90%e6%9d%be%e5%89%8d%e7%a5%9e%e6%a5%bd%e3%80%91%e5%8d%81%e4%ba%8c%e3%81%ae%e6%89%8b%e7%8d%85%e5%ad%90%e8%88%9e%e3%83%bb%e4%ba%94%e6%96%b9%e3%80%80%e5%86%99%e7%9c%9f/ |title=[Matsumae Kagura] Twelve-handed Shishi Mai & Gohō – Photographs |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref>
== Transmission == === Regions === Matsumae Kagura is transmitted in a wide area including the Japan Sea coastal regions and the Dounan area of {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido|1=Hokkaido}}, and subtle regional differences have emerged over time.<ref name=":0" /> Block preservation associations have been established in the four regions of Matsumae, Fukushima, Hakodate, and Otaru, each working to preserve and pass on its tradition.<ref name=":0" /> Performances are held at shrine festivals and local event venues throughout Hokkaido (with schedules varying by region). In Matsumae Town, a public performance of Matsumae Kagura is held annually on {{ill|April 29|en|April 29|WD=Q2535|lt=April 29|1=April 29}} at the Honmaru Plaza of {{ill|Matsumae Park|ja|松前公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Park|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 松前城|1=Matsumae Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1143974}}.<ref name=":0" /> The following is a list of municipalities where Matsumae Kagura is mainly transmitted.<ref name=":1" />
{{Columns-list|20em| * {{ill|Hakodate|en|Hakodate|WD=Q26418|lt=Hakodate City|1=Hakodate}} * {{ill|Otaru|en|Otaru|WD=Q242108|lt=Otaru City|1=Otaru}} * {{ill|Hokuto, Hokkaido|en|Hokuto, Hokkaido|WD=Q842301|lt=Hokuto City|1=Hokuto, Hokkaido}} * {{ill|Matsumae Town|ja|松前町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Town|1=松前町|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1307271}} * {{ill|Fukushima, Hokkaido|en|Fukushima, Hokkaido|WD=Q1354260|lt=Fukushima Town|1=Fukushima, Hokkaido}} * {{ill|Shiriuchi, Hokkaido|en|Shiriuchi, Hokkaido|WD=Q1354297|lt=Shiriuchi Town|1=Shiriuchi, Hokkaido}} * {{ill|Kikonai, Hokkaido|en|Kikonai, Hokkaido|WD=Q1354308|lt=Kikonai Town|1=Kikonai, Hokkaido}} * {{ill|Nanae, Hokkaido|en|Nanae, Hokkaido|WD=Q1354276|lt=Nanpō Town|1=Nanae, Hokkaido}} * === Preservation and Transmission === Matsumae Kagura was designated as an {{ill|Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|重要無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|1=National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6573893}} on March 8, {{ill|2018|en|2018|WD=Q25291|lt=2018|1=2018}}.<ref name=":0" /> It is being preserved and transmitted under the auspices of the Matsumae Kagura Hokkaido United Preservation Association, together with the Hakodate United Preservation Association, the Otaru Block Preservation Association, the Matsumae Block United Preservation Association, and the Fukushima Town Matsumae Kagura Preservation Association.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |url=https://www.siomigaoka.com/matumaekagura |title=Matsumae Kagura (Matsumae Kagura Otaru Preservation Association) |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=潮見ヶ岡神社}}</ref>
In {{ill|1958|en|1958|WD=Q5253|lt=1958|1=1958}} (Showa 33), 12 performers were designated as holders of Hokkaido's intangible cultural properties, with 4 designated in each of the three blocks (Otaru, Fukushima, and Matsumae).<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/kagura-history/ |title=About Matsumae Kagura |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> In {{ill|1968|en|1968|WD=Q2644|lt=1968|1=1968}} (Showa 43), a statewide organization called the "Matsumae Kagura United Preservation Association" was established, and subsequently in {{ill|1995|en|1995|WD=Q2068|lt=1995|1=1995}} (Heisei 7) it was selected by the national government as a "folk cultural material for which measures for documentation should be taken." To further consolidate efforts toward designation as a national intangible cultural property, the Matsumae Kagura Preservation Association was dissolved in {{ill|1999|en|1999|WD=Q2091|lt=1999|1=1999}} (Heisei 11) and replaced by the "Hokkaido Matsumae Kagura Preservation Association" (an umbrella organization comprising the Hakodate, Matsumae Block, Otaru Block, and Fukushima Town preservation associations).<ref name=":10" /> In {{ill|2008|en|2008|WD=Q2004|lt=2008|1=2008}} (Heisei 20), following the death of the last designated holder, Osamu Kimura, the designation under Hokkaido's system was cancelled; however, in June of that year a new designation was granted to the Hokkaido Matsumae Kagura United Preservation Association (covering 4 blocks). Finally, in {{ill|2018|en|2018|WD=Q25291|lt=2018|1=2018}} (Heisei 30) it was designated as a national {{ill|Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|重要無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|1=National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6573893}}.<ref name=":10" />
Below is the timeline of events leading up to its national designation:<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":10" /> * {{ill|1958|en|1958|WD=Q5253|lt=1958|1=1958}} (Showa 33) – Designated as the first Hokkaido intangible cultural property, with 12 holders recognized. * {{ill|1995|en|1995|WD=Q2068|lt=1995|1=1995}} (Heisei 7) – Selected by the national government as a "folk cultural material for which measures for documentation should be taken" (documentary selection). * {{ill|1999|en|1999|WD=Q2091|lt=1999|1=1999}} (Heisei 11) – The Matsumae Kagura United Preservation Association was formed in anticipation of national designation as an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property. * {{ill|2008|en|2008|WD=Q2004|lt=2008|1=2008}} (Heisei 20) – Following the death of the last holder, the Hokkaido designation was cancelled; subsequently, it was designated as a Hokkaido intangible folk cultural property with the preservation associations and their four subordinate groups clearly stated. * {{ill|2018|en|2018|WD=Q25291|lt=2018|1=2018}} (Heisei 30) – Designated as a national {{ill|Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|重要無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|1=National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6573893}}.

'''Matsumae Kagura''' (松前神楽) is a form of {{ill|Kagura|en|Kagura|WD=Q1348260|lt=kagura|1=Kagura}} transmitted in the coastal regions along the {{ill|Sea of Japan|en|Sea of Japan|WD=Q27092|lt=Japan Sea|1=Sea of Japan}} and in the {{ill|Dounan region|ja|道南地域|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dounan region|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido|1=Hokkaido}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=https://www.town.matsumae.hokkaido.jp/bunkazai/detail/00001640.html |title=Matsumae Kagura - まつまえの文化財 文化財一覧 |access-date=2024-11-26 |publisher=松前町教育委員会}}</ref> It is a rare type of kagura that preserves a complete repertoire of performances including the {{ill|harvesting dance|ja|採物舞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/harvesting dance|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|miko dance|ja|巫女舞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/miko dance|1=miko mai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11479841}}, {{ill|hot water ritual|ja|湯立神事|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/hot water ritual|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 湯立神楽|1=yudate kagura|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11563776}}, and {{ill|Lion dance|en|Lion dance|WD=Q713866|lt=lion dance|1=Lion dance}}, and is also distinctive in that the kagura performed by [[:en:Kannushi|Shinto priests]] includes seldom-preserved pieces such as "Chitose", {{ill|Okina|ja|翁|lt=Old Man|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okina|1=okina|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11610439}} and {{ill|Sanbasou|ja|三番叟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanbasou|1=Sanbasō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11356796}}.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/411325 |title=Matsumae Kagura - 文化遺産オンライン |access-date=2024-11-26 |publisher=文化庁}}</ref> Furthermore, the repertoire and performance style suggest connections with various kagura traditions of the {{ill|Tōhoku region|en|Tōhoku region|WD=Q129465|lt=Tohoku region|1=Tōhoku region}}.<ref name=":1" />
== Overview == Matsumae Kagura is transmitted primarily by [[:en:Kannushi|Shinto priests]] in southern {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido|1=Hokkaido}}, and encompasses a diverse range of performances including the harvesting dance of {{ill|Chokumen|ja|直面|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chokumen|1=Q119379771|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q119379771}} style, miko dance, hot water ritual, lion dance, and even masked dances such as the {{ill|Okina dance|ja|翁舞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okina dance|1=Okina-mai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11610451}}. These are performed to the accompaniment of {{ill|Drum|en|Drum|WD=Q11404|lt=taiko|1=Drum}}, {{ill|Ryūteki|en|Ryūteki|WD=Q1760249|lt=ryuteki|1=Ryūteki}}, and hand-held bells ({{ill|tehira suzu|ja|手平鉦|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tehira suzu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) on a performance space of roughly one ken square.<ref name=":1" /> Although the origins of Matsumae Kagura are not clear, there is a record from {{ill|1674|en|1674|WD=Q7620|lt=1674|1=1674}} (the 2nd year of {{ill|Enpō|en|Enpō|WD=Q1145735|lt=Empo|1=Enpō}}) indicating that a {{ill|hot water kagura|ja|湯立神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/hot water kagura|1=yudate kagura|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11563776}} was performed for the first time within {{ill|Fukuyama Castle|ja|福山城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuyama Castle|1=Q11288334|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11288334}}, and a lion head donated by the lord of the {{ill|Matsumae Domain|en|Matsumae Domain|WD=Q18669712|lt=Matsumae Domain|1=Matsumae Domain}} still exists.<ref name=":1" /> In this way, Matsumae Kagura was closely associated with the Matsumae Domain. Today, it is transmitted mainly in the {{ill|Oshima region|ja|渡島地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshima region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 渡島総合振興局|1=Oshima Subprefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2226825}}, as well as in the {{ill|Hiyama region|ja|檜山地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyama region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 檜山振興局|1=Hiyama Subprefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1142537}}, the {{ill|Shiribeshi region|ja|後志地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiribeshi region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 後志支庁|1=Shiribeshi Subprefecture (1910-2010)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q839388}}, and even in {{ill|Obira, Hokkaido|en|Obira, Hokkaido|WD=Q1348684|lt=Kodaira Town|1=Obira, Hokkaido}} in the {{ill|Rumoi region|ja|留萌地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rumoi region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 留萌振興局|1=Rumoi Subprefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1151453}}. It is performed at the annual festival ({{ill|Reisai|lt=Reisai|lt=Reitaisai|ja|例祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reitaisai|qq=}}) of about 120 {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=shrines|1=Shinto shrine}}, as well as at New Year festivals and {{ill|Funatama festivals|ja|船魂|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Funatama festivals|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 船霊|1=Q11614362|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11614362}} held at shrine {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|en|Haiden (Shinto)|WD=Q3125745|lt=worship halls|1=Haiden (Shinto)}}, and is also performed in private homes upon request for purposes such as warding off misfortune ({{ill|yaku-yoke|ja|厄除け|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yaku-yoke|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 厄祓い|1=Apotropaic magic|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q620591}}) or celebrating a new construction.<ref name=":1" /> In addition, in some areas the lion dance is performed as a New Year purification ({{ill|monbarai|ja|門祓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monbarai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) by visiting local households.<ref name=":1" />
The former {{ill|Matsumae Domain|en|Matsumae Domain|WD=Q18669712|lt=Matsumae Domain|1=Matsumae Domain}}, which once had the kagura performed within its castle (thus also called "Castle Kagura" or '''Ōjō Kagura'''), saw it vigorously performed by Shinto priests during the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}}, and it later spread widely. Today, it is transmitted in a wide area including {{ill|Hakodate|en|Hakodate|WD=Q26418|lt=Hakodate City|1=Hakodate}}, {{ill|Otaru|en|Otaru|WD=Q242108|lt=Otaru City|1=Otaru}}, {{ill|Matsumae Town|ja|松前町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Town|1=松前町|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1307271}} in {{ill|Matsumae District, Hokkaido|en|Matsumae District, Hokkaido|WD=Q1145821|lt=Matsumae District|1=Matsumae District, Hokkaido}}, and {{ill|Fukushima, Hokkaido|en|Fukushima, Hokkaido|WD=Q1354260|lt=Fukushima Town|1=Fukushima, Hokkaido}}, as well as in other parts of the Japan Sea coastal regions and the Dounan area of Hokkaido, and is publicly performed at shrine major festivals.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/137157 |title=Matsumae Kagura - 文化遺産オンライン |access-date=2024-11-26 |publisher=文化庁}}</ref>
== History == The origins of Matsumae Kagura are variously explained and remain uncertain.<ref name=":0" /> According to the official chronicle of the {{ill|Matsumae Family|ja|松前家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Family|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 蠣崎氏|1=Kakizaki clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q15734194}}, as recorded in the {{ill|Shinra no Kiroku|en|Shinra no Kiroku|WD=Q17218176|lt=Shinra no Kiroku|1=Shinra no Kiroku}}, in {{ill|1625|en|1625|WD=Q6826|lt=1625|1=1625}} (the 2nd year of {{ill|Kan'ei|en|Kan'ei|WD=Q1192913|lt=Kanei|1=Kan'ei}}) when the {{ill|Hachiman shrine|en|Hachiman shrine|WD=Q11390939|lt=Hachiman Shrine|1=Hachiman shrine}} that had been located in Ōdate was relocated to Fukuyama, records mention the construction of a treasure hall, a worship hall, and the building of a "Kaguraya" (kagura hall). Whether the kagura performed in that "Kaguraya" is the same as the Matsumae Kagura transmitted today is not certain, but it is clear that kagura was already practiced within the territory of the Matsumae Domain at that time.<ref name=":0" /> According to the "Fukuyama Hifu", in {{ill|1974|en|1974|WD=Q2478|lt=1974|1=1974}} (the 2nd year of {{ill|Enpō|en|Enpō|WD=Q1145735|lt=Empo|1=Enpō}}) during the era of the 10th lord of the Matsumae Domain, {{ill|Matsumae Norihiro|ja|松前矩廣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Norihiro|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the "Shizugama Yudate Kagura" was performed for the first time as an official event inside Fukuyama Castle. Since then, the kagura has been performed every other year in the castle’s spear hall under the patronage of the Matsumae Domain’s lord.<ref name=":0" /> Furthermore, according to the "Gojōnai Daijinji" established in {{ill|1681|en|1681|WD=Q7645|lt=1681|1=1681}} (the 9th year of {{ill|Enpō|en|Enpō|WD=Q1145735|lt=Empo|1=Enpō}}), it is evident that 23 divine rituals and dances, beginning with the "Gokito" (prayer ritual), were already in existence at that time.<ref name=":0" />
Subsequently, the kagura form was further refined, and today it is composed of 12 divine rituals and 21 dances.<ref name=":0" /> Matsumae Kagura was passed down in an hereditary manner by the shrine families within the Matsumae Domain, who strictly preserved the ancient traditions and developed the art into a dignified form of ritual performance.<ref name=":0" /> At the same time, Matsumae Kagura was greatly supported by the common people.<ref name=":0" /> People, for their own benefit, performed various kagura prayers ({{ill|kito|ja|祈祷|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祈り|1=Prayer|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q40953}}) such as the {{ill|herring field kagura|ja|ニシン場|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/herring field kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the {{ill|salmon field abundant harvest kagura|ja|鮭場豊漁神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/salmon field abundant harvest kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the {{ill|fairground safety kagura|ja|会場安全神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fairground safety kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the {{ill|small-boat new construction kagura|ja|手船新造神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/small-boat new construction kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the {{ill|fire-extinguishing kagura|ja|火災消滅神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fire-extinguishing kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the {{ill|smallpox safety kagura|ja|疱瘡安全神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/smallpox safety kagura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, wishing for safe journeys, abundant harvests, and the dispelling of epidemics.<ref name=":0" /> When the patronage of the Matsumae Domain was lost during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}}, the shrine families who had preserved Matsumae Kagura deepened their ties with the parishioners, and the tradition has been transmitted up to the present day.<ref name=":0" /> Moreover, people freed from the constraints of the feudal han system migrated throughout Hokkaido in search of abundant fishing resources, and in the midst of harsh living conditions, they established Matsumae Kagura as a familiar cultural practice from childhood in their new communities.<ref name=":0" />
Since the Meiji period, Matsumae Kagura has been performed throughout the Japan Sea coastal regions, especially in the {{ill|Oshima region|ja|渡島地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshima region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 渡島総合振興局|1=Oshima Subprefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2226825}}.<ref name=":0" /> However, over time, subtle regional differences have emerged in Matsumae Kagura.<ref name=":0" /> Today, block preservation associations have been formed in the four regions of Matsumae, Fukushima, Hakodate, and Otaru, each working to preserve and transmit its unique tradition.<ref name=":0" /> On March 8, {{ill|2018|en|2018|WD=Q25291|lt=2018|1=2018}}, it was designated as an {{ill|Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|重要無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|1=National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6573893}}.<ref name=":0" />
== Repertoire == [[File:Kuruma_okina_mai.jpg|alt=翁舞（The image is not of Matsumae Kagura but of the Kuruma Okina Mai [ja]）|thumb]] The repertoire of Matsumae Kagura is extensive, as listed below. Although the content and names of the pieces vary slightly between transmission areas, all share a strong ritual and ceremonial character with minimal emphasis on mere entertainment.<ref name=":2" /> It is said that because the former lord of the Matsumae Domain was originally from the {{ill|Wakasa region|ja|若狭地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 嶺南|1=Reinan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11477418}} of {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|en|Fukui Prefecture|WD=Q133879|lt=Fukui Prefecture|1=Fukui Prefecture}}, there are connections with the dance music of Kyoto and the kagura of the {{ill|Izumo region|ja|出雲地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 出雲|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}}, and also direct influences from the mountain ascetic kagura and variety performances of the {{ill|Tōhoku region|en|Tōhoku region|WD=Q129465|lt=Tohoku region|1=Tōhoku region}}.<ref name=":2" /> Thus, Matsumae Kagura, which has preserved a tradition in Hokkaido since the Edo period and has been widely performed with regional characteristics added throughout the island, is an important example illustrating the evolution of performing arts and regional traits.<ref name=":2" />
* '''Sakaki Mai''' (さかきまい) – A dance in which the officiant moves gracefully to the right, left, forward, and backward while performing in a quiet manner, symbolically purifying the sacred precinct by entering the inner court of the shrine in the morning and evening, and offering the {{ill|Gohei|en|Gohei|WD=Q1011372|lt=gohei|1=Gohei}} as an expression of divine service by the Shinto priest.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/%e6%9d%be%e5%89%8d%e7%a5%9e%e6%a5%bd%e3%83%bb%e8%b1%86%e7%9f%a5%e8%ad%98%e3%80%80%e6%a6%8a%e8%88%9e%ef%bc%88%e3%81%95%e3%81%8b%e3%81%8d%e3%81%be%e3%81%84%ef%bc%89/ |title=Matsumae Kagura – Tidbits: Sakaki Mai (さかきまい) |access-date=2024-11-28 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> In various regions, it is also called "Heihaku Mai" or "Norito Mai". This kagura was personally developed by the Matsumae Domain and its lord.<ref name=":3" /> * '''Suzue''' (すずあげ) – A dance in which the dancer holds a {{ill|bell|ja|鈴|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/bell|1=suzu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q7651136}} and a {{ill|fan|ja|扇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fan|1=Q108778988|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108778988}}, frequently raising and lowering the bell during the performance; it is said to depict the descent of a {{ill|celestial maiden|ja|天女|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/celestial maiden|qq=}}. As it is performed by girls under their teenage years, it is also known as "Otome Mai" or "Miko Mai".<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-155/ |title=Matsumae Kagura – Tidbits: Suzue (Miko Dance) |access-date=2024-11-28 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''Fukuden Mai''' (ふくでんまい) – A dance in which the performer holds sacred banners in both hands and purifies all four corners. Accompanied by the shout "Haayo!" the dancer treads on fields to symbolize solidifying them while praying for a bountiful harvest of the five grains. It is also known as "Atoharai" because it is performed at the end of evening festivals where a lion dance is not held.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-109/ |title=Matsumae Kagura – Tidbits: Fukuden Mai (ふくでんまい) |access-date=2024-11-28 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> The music and divine songs of Fukuden Mai are also used in other pieces. * '''Niwa Sagomai''' (にわさごまい) – Also known as "Niwa Sangomai" or "Torianakomai", this dance portrays a rooster, considered a sacred bird that heralds the opening of the heavenly rock door to announce the arrival of light after darkness, and that treads firmly upon the earth at the beginning of the world ({{ill|Zuitori|ja|瑞鳥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zuitori|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 瑞獣|1=Q11573922|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11573922}}). The dancer wears a crown with two bird figures (male and female); the male’s feathers symbolize auspicious clouds (heaven) and the female’s represent ocean waves (earth), expressing the harmony between the sexes and celebrating a peaceful world by scattering the divine rice that signifies the abundant harvest of the "land of the auspicious grain" lasting fifteen hundred autumns.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-1571/ |title=Matsumae Kagura on a luxury liner – Niwa Sagomai |access-date=2024-11-18 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''Shika Sagomai''' (しかさごまい) – A dance performed when a shrine’s buildings or its {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|WD=Q234731|lt=torii|1=Torii}} are newly constructed. It is a custom mainly found in southern Hokkaido and is also called "Sanpin Mai" or "Sanshu Mai".<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-1484/ |title=[Video] Matsumae Kagura Joint Performance – Shika Sagomai |access-date=2024-11-28 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''Sanbasou Mai''' (さんばそうまい) – A dance performed by a short, dark-faced, vigorous old man who symbolizes robust health, longevity, and moral rectitude. He celebrates his own long life and the prosperity of his family by dancing joyfully in honor of his talented descendants, blessing the flourishing of his lineage.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-1549/ |title=Matsumae Kagura on a luxury liner – Sanbasou Mai |access-date=2024-11-28 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''Okina Mai''' (翁舞) – A dance in which a humorous, tall, and gentle old man, despite his wrinkled forehead, demonstrates physical strength acquired over many years, and during the performance expresses his wishes in words, celebrating longevity, career success, and prosperity, embodying the blessings of the deities of longevity and fortune.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-1574/ |title=Matsumae Kagura on a luxury liner – Okina Mai |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''Kami Asobi Mai''' (かみあそびまい) – A dance in which two warriors armed with bows and arrows expel malevolent spirits from all directions and restore a rightful state of mind. It was intended to demonstrate the virtue of the Matsumae Domain both internally and externally, and to pray for the pacification of {{ill|Ezo|en|Ezo|WD=Q1040184|lt=Ezochi|1=Ezo}} and universal peace. This dance is traditionally attributed to the 6th lord of the Matsumae Domain, {{ill|Matsumae Norihiro|ja|矩広|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Norihiro|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and is also known as "Tenno Asobi Mai".<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |url=https://gongensan.jp/KAGURA/%E6%9D%BE%E5%89%8D%E7%A5%9E%E6%A5%BD-%E5%85%B6%E3%83%8E%E4%BA%8C/ |title=Matsumae Kagura, Part II |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=権現山内浦神社}}</ref> * '''Shichigosan Harai Mai''' (しめはらいまい) – A dance in which a sword is used to purify all four directions, symbolically expelling evil spirits.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/post-129/ |title=Fukushima Town/ Shirofu Ōjin Shrine Festival: Matsumae Kagura "Shichigosan Harai Mai" (Heisei 19) |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> * '''{{ill|Lion dance|en|Lion dance|WD=Q713866|lt=Shishi Mai|1=Lion dance}}''' (ししまい) – A lion dance that exists in various forms such as "Twelve-handed Shishi Mai", "Onryōi Mai", "Gohō", "Shishi no Suzuage", and "Men Ashi Shishi (Sasara)".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/%e3%80%90%e6%9d%be%e5%89%8d%e7%a5%9e%e6%a5%bd%e3%80%91%e5%8d%81%e4%ba%8c%e3%81%ae%e6%89%8b%e7%8d%85%e5%ad%90%e8%88%9e%e3%83%bb%e4%ba%94%e6%96%b9%e3%80%80%e5%86%99%e7%9c%9f/ |title=[Matsumae Kagura] Twelve-handed Shishi Mai & Gohō – Photographs |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref>
== Transmission == === Regions === Matsumae Kagura is transmitted in a wide area including the Japan Sea coastal regions and the Dounan area of {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido|1=Hokkaido}}, and subtle regional differences have emerged over time.<ref name=":0" /> Block preservation associations have been established in the four regions of Matsumae, Fukushima, Hakodate, and Otaru, each working to preserve and pass on its tradition.<ref name=":0" /> Performances are held at shrine festivals and local event venues throughout Hokkaido (with schedules varying by region). In Matsumae Town, a public performance of Matsumae Kagura is held annually on {{ill|April 29|en|April 29|WD=Q2535|lt=April 29|1=April 29}} at the Honmaru Plaza of {{ill|Matsumae Park|ja|松前公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumae Park|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 松前城|1=Matsumae Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1143974}}.<ref name=":0" /> The following is a list of municipalities where Matsumae Kagura is mainly transmitted.<ref name=":1" />

=== Preservation and Transmission === Matsumae Kagura was designated as an {{ill|Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|重要無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|1=National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6573893}} on March 8, {{ill|2018|en|2018|WD=Q25291|lt=2018|1=2018}}.<ref name=":0" /> It is being preserved and transmitted under the auspices of the Matsumae Kagura Hokkaido United Preservation Association, together with the Hakodate United Preservation Association, the Otaru Block Preservation Association, the Matsumae Block United Preservation Association, and the Fukushima Town Matsumae Kagura Preservation Association.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |url=https://www.siomigaoka.com/matumaekagura |title=Matsumae Kagura (Matsumae Kagura Otaru Preservation Association) |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=潮見ヶ岡神社}}</ref>
In {{ill|1958|en|1958|WD=Q5253|lt=1958|1=1958}} (Showa 33), 12 performers were designated as holders of Hokkaido's intangible cultural properties, with 4 designated in each of the three blocks (Otaru, Fukushima, and Matsumae).<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |url=https://yokisourou.com/kagura-history/ |title=About Matsumae Kagura |access-date=2024-11-29 |publisher=良き候北加伊道}}</ref> In {{ill|1968|en|1968|WD=Q2644|lt=1968|1=1968}} (Showa 43), a statewide organization called the "Matsumae Kagura United Preservation Association" was established, and subsequently in {{ill|1995|en|1995|WD=Q2068|lt=1995|1=1995}} (Heisei 7) it was selected by the national government as a "folk cultural material for which measures for documentation should be taken." To further consolidate efforts toward designation as a national intangible cultural property, the Matsumae Kagura Preservation Association was dissolved in {{ill|1999|en|1999|WD=Q2091|lt=1999|1=1999}} (Heisei 11) and replaced by the "Hokkaido Matsumae Kagura Preservation Association" (an umbrella organization comprising the Hakodate, Matsumae Block, Otaru Block, and Fukushima Town preservation associations).<ref name=":10" /> In {{ill|2008|en|2008|WD=Q2004|lt=2008|1=2008}} (Heisei 20), following the death of the last designated holder, Osamu Kimura, the designation under Hokkaido's system was cancelled; however, in June of that year a new designation was granted to the Hokkaido Matsumae Kagura United Preservation Association (covering 4 blocks). Finally, in {{ill|2018|en|2018|WD=Q25291|lt=2018|1=2018}} (Heisei 30) it was designated as a national {{ill|Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|重要無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|1=National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6573893}}.<ref name=":10" />
Below is the timeline of events leading up to its national designation:<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":10" /> * {{ill|1958|en|1958|WD=Q5253|lt=1958|1=1958}} (Showa 33) – Designated as the first Hokkaido intangible cultural property, with 12 holders recognized. * {{ill|1995|en|1995|WD=Q2068|lt=1995|1=1995}} (Heisei 7) – Selected by the national government as a "folk cultural material for which measures for documentation should be taken" (documentary selection). * {{ill|1999|en|1999|WD=Q2091|lt=1999|1=1999}} (Heisei 11) – The Matsumae Kagura United Preservation Association was formed in anticipation of national designation as an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property. * {{ill|2008|en|2008|WD=Q2004|lt=2008|1=2008}} (Heisei 20) – Following the death of the last holder, the Hokkaido designation was cancelled; subsequently, it was designated as a Hokkaido intangible folk cultural property with the preservation associations and their four subordinate groups clearly stated. * {{ill|2018|en|2018|WD=Q25291|lt=2018|1=2018}} (Heisei 30) – Designated as a national {{ill|Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|重要無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|1=National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6573893}}.
